Butler was born in [Truckee, California](/wiki/Truckee,_California "Truckee, California"), and raised in [The Woodlands, Texas](/wiki/The_Woodlands,_Texas "The Woodlands, Texas"), with a [Latter-Day Saint](/wiki/Mormons "Mormons") upbringing.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6) He lived in [Buenos Aires](/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires"), Argentina, before his brother [Will](/wiki/Will_Butler_(musician) "Will Butler (musician)") was born.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

His father, Edwin Farnham Butler II, worked as a geologist for oil conglomerate [Halliburton](/wiki/Halliburton "Halliburton") in [Houston, Texas](/wiki/Houston,_Texas "Houston, Texas").[[8]](#cite_note-8) His mother, Liza Rey, who performed on the family TV show, *[The King Family Show](/wiki/The_King_Family_Show "The King Family Show")*, plays jazz harp and sings. Butler's parents currently live on [Mount Desert Island, Maine](/wiki/Mount_Desert_Island "Mount Desert Island").[[9]](#cite_note-9) Butler's maternal grandfather was [jazz](/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") [steel guitarist](/wiki/Steel_guitar "Steel guitar") [Alvino Rey](/wiki/Alvino_Rey "Alvino Rey"), a pioneer bandleader whose career spanned eight decades.[[10]](#cite_note-10) His maternal grandmother, Luise, was a member of [The King Sisters](/wiki/The_King_Sisters "The King Sisters"), who starred in a weekly variety program on [ABC](/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") called *The King Family Show*.

At the age of 15, Butler started attending the [Phillips Exeter Academy](/wiki/Phillips_Exeter_Academy "Phillips Exeter Academy") preparatory school in [New Hampshire](/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire"), where he lived in [Abbot Hall](/wiki/Abbot_Hall_(Phillips_Exeter_Academy) "Abbot Hall (Phillips Exeter Academy)").[[11]](#cite_note-11) After graduation, he studied photography and creative writing at [Sarah Lawrence College](/wiki/Sarah_Lawrence_College "Sarah Lawrence College"), but left after a year.

Crocus :: Taxonomy :: Phylogeny :: chunk_0009
The genus *Crocus* belongs to the [monocot](/wiki/Monocotyledon "Monocotyledon") [family](/wiki/Family_(biology) "Family (biology)") [Iridaceae](/wiki/Iridaceae "Iridaceae") (iris family), specifically the large subfamily [Crocoideae](/wiki/Crocoideae "Crocoideae"). Within that subfamily, crocus is placed on the [tribe](/wiki/Tribe_(biology) "Tribe (biology)"), Ixieae (synonym Croceae),[[b]](#cite_note-52) one of five. The Ixieae are then subdivided into subtribes, with the genera *Crocus*, *[Romulea](/wiki/Romulea "Romulea")* and *[Syringodea](/wiki/Syringodea "Syringodea")* forming subtribe Romuleinae. The Romuleinae have been characterised within the Ixieae by progressively reduced aerial stems.[[51]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldblatt_et_al1998312-53) solitary flowers on the stem branches and woody tunics on the corms. They also often have divided style branches. However, *Crocus* corm tunics are fibrous and membranous rather than woody as in *Syringodea.* Also, *Crocus* has a ridged and often keeled abaxial leaf surface, while that of *Syringodea* is rounded, and the midline adaxial translucency of *Crocus* is lacking in *Syringodea*. *[Romulea](/wiki/Romulea "Romulea")* is principally distinguished from the other two genera by generally having aerial stems or at least an ovary at ground level, compared with the other acaulescent genera, other differences include unifacial rather than bifacial leaves and the pollen structure.[[52]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPhillipsRix198931-54)[[51]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldblatt_et_al1998312-53)

Within the Romuleinae, *Crocus* is a [sister group](/wiki/Sister_group "Sister group") to *Syringodea*, the two genera forming a sister group to *Romulea*.[[49]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldblatt_et_al2006-50)[[53]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPetersen_et_al2008-55)[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarpke_et_al2013-15)

On 9 October 2014, the [Swedish Academy](/wiki/Swedish_Academy "Swedish Academy") announced that that year's [Nobel Prize in Literature](/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature") was awarded to Patrick Modiano "for the art of memory with which he has evoked the most ungraspable human destinies and uncovered the life-world of the occupation."[[19]](#cite_note-19) Modiano was the 15th French writer to be awarded the prize.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

Though Modiano was the fourth favourite on [Ladbrokes](/wiki/Ladbrokes "Ladbrokes") to win the 2014 Nobel Prize,[[21]](#cite_note-guard-21) the choice of Modiano was described as unexpected.[[22]](#cite_note-22) Modiano himself found it unexpected, but said he was "touched" by the recognition.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

At the award ceremony in Stockholm on 10 December 2014, [Jesper Svenbro](/wiki/Jesper_Svenbro "Jesper Svenbro") of the Swedish Academy said:

> In novel upon novel Modiano has developed his ability to use almost non-existent documentation – old telephone numbers, street addresses – to endow the past with entrancing life and his Parisian cityscape with a singular voice. Magnificently, his work instantiates what an earlier Nobel Laureate, [Seamus Heaney](/wiki/Seamus_Heaney "Seamus Heaney"), called “the poetry of place”.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

Harvard was founded and authorized by the [Massachusetts General Court](/wiki/Massachusetts_General_Court#Massachusetts_Bay_Colony "Massachusetts General Court"), the governing legislature of [colonial](/wiki/Colonial_history_of_the_United_States "Colonial history of the United States")-era [Massachusetts Bay Colony](/wiki/Massachusetts_Bay_Colony "Massachusetts Bay Colony").[[13]](#cite_note-13) While never formally affiliated with any [Protestant denomination](/wiki/Protestant_church "Protestant church"), Harvard trained [Congregational](/wiki/Congregationalism_in_the_United_States "Congregationalism in the United States") clergy until its curriculum and student body were gradually secularized in the 18th century. In 1780, the [Constitution of Massachusetts](/wiki/Constitution_of_Massachusetts "Constitution of Massachusetts") referred to it as a [university](/wiki/University "University"), and a new [medical school](/wiki/Medical_school "Medical school") established in 1782 was named the [Medical Institution of Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_Medical_School "Harvard Medical School"); but this was a new name, not a new foundation.
